The install wrapper re-rendered through installArgv and run with a stand-in agent against this checkout's freshly packed tarballs (sjawhar-pi-legion-9.6.1.tgz declaring 24, sjawhar-pi-envoy-9.5.1.tgz): `2 packages installed`, the agent started with the two generation-directory --extension roots, `installed pi-legion 9.6.1 contract 24 | pi-envoy 9.5.1`, and `legion probe-image` on that installed pair printed `probe-image: OK … daemon-api-version=24`; the published pi-legion 9.6.1 (contract 23) by registry URL was refused `declares daemon API contract 23; this daemon requires 24` before exec. The daemon lanes the implementer named re-ran green here: `internal/api -run 'Stale|Undecodable|OperatorBearer|WrongSecret'`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 internal/supervise -run 'StalePlugin|Plugin|Stale'`, the eight `internal/daemon` tests plus TestRunPrunesTheSecretFilesOfClaimsWithNoProcess (which the implementer's pod could not run), `internal/store`, `internal/projection`, `cmd/legion`. `legion version` (one line plain, two lines linked) and `legion start --check-config` (none / from the binary / from legion.yaml, and every refusal) reproduced as recorded. The proof holds for what it exercised; it never exercised an exact-version source — the documented form and the release-linked pair — which is where the change breaks (failures[0]).

failures.criterion: 4. Under Kubernetes the pod stays and the plugin comes from npm: Oh My Pi loads pi-legion and pi-envoy at the exact versions the daemon named — and the Errors row 'The install fails … charged as a launch failure … The launch budget ends a lasting failure in a worker-died'
failures.evidence: An exact-version source never installs. `runtime.kubernetes.plugins: {pi_legion: 9.6.1, pi_envoy: 9.5.1}` is accepted by the loader (`legion start --check-config` → `plugins: @sjawhar/pi-legion 9.6.1 @sjawhar/pi-envoy 9.5.1 (from legion.yaml)`, exit 0), and a binary built with `-X main.piLegionVersion=9.6.1 -X main.piEnvoyVersion=9.5.1` — the shape release.yaml links (`$PI_LEGION_VERSION` is the bare published version) — prints the same pair `(from the binary)`; ResolvedPlugins hands both to specs.SpawnSpec unchanged, and installScript (internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins.go) renders `/usr/local/bin/bun add --exact '9.6.1' '9.5.1'`. Run in this pod with a stand-in agent, bun answers `error: Package "9.6.1" with tag "latest" not found, but package exists` / `error: 9.6.1@ failed to resolve` (and the same for 9.5.1), the wrapper prints `legion plugins: installing 9.6.1 and 9.5.1 failed` and exits 1 before `exec` — no `AGENT STARTED`. A bare version is a package name to `bun add`; only `@sjawhar/pi-legion@9.6.1` names the package at a version. Tarball paths and http(s) URLs (what the implementer's proof and stage 4a's checkpoint use) work, so neither caught it. Consequence under production's default source, the release-linked pair: at the first boot every live claim is relaunched, every install fails before Oh My Pi starts, the launcher reports the child gone, each death is charged, and the launch budget ends every live role in `worker-died` — the fleet-wide stall this change exists to prevent. Red test: `cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox -run 'TestAVersionSourceIsInstalledAsThePackageAtThatVersion|TestATarballOrURLSourceReachesBunVerbatim' -count=1 -v` → `plugins_test.go:158: bun add was asked for ["add" "--exact" "9.7.0" "9.6.1"], want @sjawhar/pi-legion@9.7.0 and @sjawhar/pi-envoy@9.6.1` (FAIL); the companion test holds a tarball path and a URL verbatim (PASS, and must stay so after the fix). Both run the rendered script under sh with a stand-in bun at the script's own bun path and read the words bun receives. After the fix, docs/kubernetes.md's `bun add --exact <pi-legion source> <pi-envoy source>` sentence (Contract discipline) and the stage 4a checkpoint, which installs tarballs only, should say/exercise the version form too (pi-envoy 9.5.1 by version would do until a pi-legion at contract 24 is published).

observations: Self-healing extra round-trip: a pod whose image is still the old one (the operator restarted the daemon on the new release before pinning the new image) loads the image's old plugin at every launch that carries no Plugins — a death relaunch after the role registered at 24, or a fresh claim's first launch — so such a launch registers stale once, is answered 409 and relaunched uncharged with the install, then registers at 24. Each converges in two launches; noted for the reviewer, not a defect against the spec.
